references.text: The angel Gabriel greets Mary with the words "Hail, you who have received grace" – a blessing of her who was chosen to bear Christ, just as the woman in the crowd blesses the one who bore Jesus ([ref:Luk 1:28|Luke 1:28]).

Elizabeth blesses Mary: "Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!" and "Blessed is she who believed." This is a direct parallel to the woman's blessing of Jesus' mother in [ref:Luk 1:42-45|Luke 1:42-45].
Mary prophesies in her song that "all generations will call me blessed," which is reflected in the woman's spontaneous blessing of the one who bore Jesus ([ref:Luk 1:48|Luke 1:48]).

Jesus' answer in the next verse corrects and expands on the woman's blessing: "Blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it." Jesus shifts the focus from physical motherhood to spiritual obedience ([ref:Luk 11:28|Luke 11:28]).

Jesus defines his true family: "My mother and my brothers, these are they who hear the word of God and do it." This corresponds with Jesus' redirection of the physical blessing in Luke 11:27 toward spiritual obedience ([ref:Luk 8:19-21|Luke 8:19-21]).

A contrast to the blessing of the womb that bore Jesus: on the way to the cross, Jesus says "Blessed are the barren, the wombs that have not borne, and the breasts that have not nursed." Where the woman blesses the womb that bore him, Jesus reverses the image in the face of judgment ([ref:Luk 23:29|Luke 23:29]).

Jesus points to his disciples and says: "Whoever does the will of my heavenly Father is my brother and sister and mother." Here too, Jesus redefines physical kinship as a spiritual relationship based on obedience to God's will ([ref:Matt 12:46-50|Matthew 12:46-50]).

Wisdom says: "Blessed are those who listen to me … Blessed is the person who listens to me." The blessing associated with listening to wisdom forms the background for Jesus' point that true blessedness lies in hearing and keeping God's word ([ref:Ordsp 8:32-34|Proverbs 8:32-34]).
